newsitem.title: USA: US stocks seen higher but volatility fears remain.
newsitem.headline: US stocks seen higher but volatility fears remain.

text.p: U.S. stocks were expected to open cautiously higher Tuesday ahead of the afternoon meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee, but analysts warned of continued volatility set off by end-of-year profit-takiing.

While the Fed was widely expected to leave interest rates unchanged, the expiration of options Friday and the desire to lock in profits could spur a new round of volatility, warned Peter Cardillo, research director at Westfalia Investments.
"Today I suspect a higher opening, but I would be very cautious...We could see selling develop later in the session, (but) I don't think we will break under 6200," Cardillo said.
"As we approach Christmas I think the annual so-called Santa rally is going to be a little more difficult to achieve this year, since the market has gone up so much," he added.

Prudential Securities market analyst Hildegarde Zagorski said "I would expect a steady open. Everything in Europe looks fairly stable except for Germany." She saw greater stability in technology after the drubbing the sector took Monday.
On Monday, profit-taking in technology stocks sent the Nasdaq Composite Index hurtling lower for its steepest decline since July 23.

"I think we are seeing a market that is obviously in a rotation process where people are beginning to lock in profits in those groups that have gone up substantially such as technology stocks," Cardillo said.
But he warned: "I see a continued increase in volatility, with gyrations from 100 to 150 points being common."

"I would look at banking stocks if we get another decline in the market...others to watch are the basic industries such as metals, steel companies...energy stocks might run counter to any market declines," he said.
In Tokyo, the Nikkei 225 share index ended marginally lower, off 8.58 points or 0.04 percent to 20,413.46. Gains in areas such as construction and banking offset earlier losses.
London stocks were lower, off almost 16 to 3978 in afternoon trading.
